name: test

entries.name: Mortal Nature
entries: Your creature type is Humanoid.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: Blessed by divine power, you can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light and in darkness as if it were dim light.

entries.name: Age
entries: Hochlings mature at the same rate as Children but often live slightly longer.

entries.name: Alignment
entries: The blood of the gods does not dictate destiny. Hochlings can be found among every alignment, though many feel pressure to embody the ideals associated with their divine ancestor.

entries.name: Size
entries: Hochlings are about the same size and build as Children. Your size is Medium or Small.

entries.name: Speed
entries: Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

entries.name: Celestial Resistance
entries: You have resistance to radiant and necrotic damage.

entries.name: Healing Hands
entries: As an action, you can touch a creature and restore a number of d4s equal to your proficiency bonus. The creature regains a number of hit points equal to the total rolled. Once you use this trait, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

entries.name: Divine Spark
entries: Choose one Cleric cantrip. The cantrip should reflect the nature of the deity or divine power from which your bloodline descends. Wisdom, Intelligence, or Charisma (chosen when you gain this trait) is your spellcasting ability for it.

entries.name: Languages
entries: You can speak, read, and write Common (General and one dialect) and Celestial.

entries.name: Divine Manifestation
entries: The divine essence within every Hochling manifests differently. The manifestation reflects the deity, divine domain, or divine power from which your lineage descends.
You gain one Channel Divinity option from an approved Cleric Domain. You can use that Channel Divinity once, and regain the ability to do so when you finish a short or long rest.

items: If the Channel Divinity refers to your Cleric level, use your character level instead.
If the Channel Divinity requires a saving throw, the DC equals: {@b 8 + your proficiency bonus + your choice of Wisdom, Intelligence, or Charisma} (chosen when you gain this trait).

entries: Examples of suitable manifestations include those associated with the Trickery, Light, Grave, War, Peace, Order, Knowledge, Nature, Forge, Death, Beauty, Blood, Time, Madness, Lust, and Darkness domains.
Alternatively, you may choose the traditional Aasimar transformation feature instead of a Channel Divinity.

_.displayName: holy symbol (a gift to you when you entered the priesthood)

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: A {@item holy symbol|phb} (a gift to you when you entered the priesthood), a prayer {@item book|phb} or prayer wheel, 5 sticks of incense, vestments, a set of {@item common clothes|phb}, and a belt {@item pouch|phb} containing 15 gp

entries.name: Feature: Shelter of the Faithful
entries: As an acolyte, you command the respect of those who share your faith, and you can perform the religious ceremonies of your deity. You and your adventuring companions can expect to receive free healing and care at a temple, shrine, or other established presence of your faith, though you must provide any material components needed for spells. Those who share your religion will support you (but only you) at a modest lifestyle.

You might also have ties to a specific temple dedicated to your chosen deity or pantheon, and you have a residence there. This could be the temple where you used to serve, if you remain on good terms with it, or a temple where you have found a new home. While near your temple, you can call upon the priests for assistance, provided the assistance you ask for is not hazardous and you remain in good standing with your temple.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Acolytes are shaped by their experience in temples or other religious communities. Their study of the history and tenets of their faith and their relationships to temples, shrines, or hierarchies affect their mannerisms and ideals. Their flaws might be some hidden hypocrisy or heretical idea, or an ideal or bond taken to an extreme.

rows: I idolize a particular hero of my faith, and constantly refer to that person's deeds and example.
I can find common ground between the fiercest enemies, empathizing with them and always working toward peace.
I see omens in every event and action. The gods try to speak to us, we just need to listen.
Nothing can shake my optimistic attitude.
I quote (or misquote) sacred texts and proverbs in almost every situation.
I am tolerant (or intolerant) of other faiths and respect (or condemn) the worship of other gods.
I've enjoyed fine food, drink, and high society among my temple's elite. Rough living grates on me.
I've spent so long in the temple that I have little practical experience dealing with people in the outside world.
Tradition. The ancient traditions of worship and sacrifice must be preserved and upheld. (Lawful)
Charity. I always try to help those in need, no matter what the personal cost. (Good)
Change. We must help bring about the changes the gods are constantly working in the world. (Chaotic)
Power. I hope to one day rise to the top of my faith's religious hierarchy. (Lawful)
Faith. I trust that my deity will guide my actions. I have faith that if I work hard, things will go well. (Lawful)
Aspiration. I seek to prove myself worthy of my god's favor by matching my actions against his or her teachings. (Any)
I would die to recover an ancient relic of my faith that was lost long ago.
I will someday get revenge on the corrupt temple hierarchy who branded me a heretic.
I owe my life to the priest who took me in when my parents died.
Everything I do is for the common people.
I will do anything to protect the temple where I served.
I seek to preserve a sacred text that my enemies consider heretical and seek to destroy.
I judge others harshly, and myself even more severely.
I put too much trust in those who wield power within my temple's hierarchy.
My piety sometimes leads me to blindly trust those that profess faith in my god.
I am inflexible in my thinking.
I am suspicious of strangers and expect the worst of them.
Once I pick a goal, I become obsessed with it to the detriment of everything else in my life.

optionalFeatures.name: Soul Eater
entries: When you burn a seal on an interdicted creature, you can activate this boon (no action required) to gain temporary hit points equal to your illrigger level.

optionalFeatures.name: Lies
entries: You can choose one type of melee weapon, such as a battleaxe, greatsword, or spear. When you attack with that type of weapon, you can use your Charisma modifier, instead of Strength or Dexterity, for the attack and damage rolls. You can choose a new weapon type, which replaces your previous choice, when you finish a long rest.

optionalFeatures.name: Stylish Tumble
entries: {@b Bonus Action (2 Stamina Points)}. As a bonus action, you can move through a hostile creature's space. Make a Charisma (Performance) check contested by the creature's Strength (Athletics) check. If you succeed, you can move through its space, and your movement for the rest of the turn does not provoke opportunity attacks from that creature.

optionalFeatures.name: Socialite Stance
entries: {@b Bonus Action (1 Stamina Point)}. As a bonus action, you adopt a charming and persuasive demeanor. While in this stance during combat, you gain a bonus to Charisma (Persuasion) checks equal to your proficiency bonus. This stance lasts until you are {@condition incapacitated|tgtt} or use a bonus action to end it.

optionalFeatures.name: Necrotic Grip
entries: {@b Reaction (2 Stamina Points)}. Your grip can wither flesh from bone. When you are grappling an opponent, you can use your reaction to deal necrotic damage equal to {@dice 1d8} + your Charisma modifier in place of basic melee damage.

optionalFeatures.name: Wink and Smile
entries: {@b Bonus Action (2 Stamina Points)}. A tossed rose, a blown kiss—you acknowledge someone whose eye was caught by your swagger. Choose one creature within 30 feet that can see you. Make a Performance check against the creature’s passive Insight. On a success, the creature is fixated on you until the start of your next turn.

optionalFeatures.name: Veil of Lies
entries: As a bonus action, you can expend a seal to become {@condition invisible} for 10 minutes or until you attack or cast a spell.

optionalFeatures.name: Mistfade Retreat
entries: {@b Reaction (2 Stamina Points)}. As your foe’s deadly attack falls upon you, your form becomes mist and shadow. When you take damage from a melee attack, you can move 15 feet without provoking opportunity attacks.

optionalFeatures.name: To My Side
entries: {@b Action (2 Stamina Points)}. You beckon someone to your side with infectious fervor, be they stranger or comrade-in-arms. Choose one conscious non-hostile creature within 30 feet of you that can see you. The creature can use its reaction to move up to its Speed in a straight line toward you. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks. If the creature enters your reach, you can use your reaction to draw one item and administer it to the creature if it is willing. The item must be a potion, medicine, or some other beneficial consumable.

cantripsKnown.name: Light
cantripsKnown.components: V, M (a firefly or phosphorescent moss)

wrapped.name: Finesse
entries: When making an attack with a finesse weapon, you use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

item.name: Shield
entries: A shield is made from wood or metal and is carried in one hand. Wielding a shield increases your Armor Class by 2. You can benefit from only one shield at a time.

item.name: Chain Shirt
entries: Made of interlocking metal rings, a chain shirt is worn between layers of clothing or leather. This armor offers modest protection to the wearer's upper body and allows the sound of the rings rubbing against one another to be muffled by outer layers.

item.name: Priest's Pack
entries: Includes:

wrapped.name: Thrown
entries: If a weapon has the thrown property, you can throw the weapon to make a ranged attack. If the weapon is a melee weapon, you use the same ability modifier for that attack roll and damage roll that you would use for a melee attack with the weapon. For example, if you throw a handaxe, you use your Strength, but if you throw a dagger, you can use either your Strength or your Dexterity, since the dagger has the finesse property.

features.name: Baleful Interdict
features.description:
You gain the ability to censure creatures with the power of Hell. Once on your turn, you can place a magical seal on a creature within 30 feet of you. You can either place this seal when you hit that target with a weapon attack (no action required), or you can use a bonus action to place this seal on a target you can see within range. This seal lasts for 1 minute or until burned (see "Burning Seals" below). A creature with one or more of your seals is referred to as an interdicted creature. Seals you place are invisible to other creatures, and when you can see an interdicted creature, the seals appear to you as glowing glyphs on the creature's body.

You can only place a limited number of seals before resting, and you regain all seals when you finish a short or long rest. The number of seals you can place increases as you gain illrigger levels, as indicated in the Seals column of the Illrigger table.

If an interdicted creature dies, you can use a bonus action on your turn to move all seals placed on them to a new creature you can see within 30 feet of them. Each seal's duration continues to elapse when an interdicted creature dies and when that seal is moved to a new creature.

Burning Seals. When an interdicted creature you can see within 30 feet of you takes damage from any source other than a seal burned by an illrigger, you can burn any number of seals you placed on them to deal 1d6 fire or necrotic damage (your choice) to that creature per seal burned. You deal this damage immediately after the triggering damage. Burning a seal doesn't require an action from you, but you can't do so while incapacitated. Once a seal is burned, it immediately vanishes.

Once you reach 5th level in this class, your connection to your archdevil strengthens. Each burned seal deals an extra 1d6 damage, for a total of 2d6. The damage of each seal increases again by 1d6 when you reach 11th level (for a total of 3d6) and 20th level (for a total of 4d6) in this class, as indicated in the Seal Damage column of the Illrigger table.

Interdict Save. Class features you gain later can add additional effects to your Baleful Interdict and require your target to make a saving throw to resist them. The saving throw DC for these effects uses your interdict save DC, which is calculated as follows:

Interdict save DC = 8 + Charisma modifier + Proficiency Bonus

features.name: Forked Tongue
features.description:
You can instinctively speak, read, and write Infernal.

In addition, you can speak two other languages of your choice, but you can't read or write them. When you finish a long rest, you can draw on your archdevil's knowledge to replace one of these two languages. When you do, choose another language whose name you know; you magically forget the previous language and gain this new one instead. Once you replace a language in this way, you must finish a long rest before you can do so again.

Starting at 9th level, this feature grants you another language, for a total of three (in addition to Infernal). Furthermore, you gain advantage on Wisdom (Insight) checks made to ascertain the intentions or sincerity of creatures.

features.name: Combat Methods
entries: At 2nd level, your infernal training expands into combat methods—martial techniques fueled by hellish stamina.

items: {@b Choose Traditions.} Gain proficiency in two combat traditions from {@filter Eldritch Blackguard|optionalfeatures|feature type=CTM:EB}, {@filter Gallant Heart|optionalfeatures|feature type=CTM:GH}, or {@filter Sanguine Knot|optionalfeatures|feature type=CTM:SK}. Learn two methods from traditions you're proficient with.
{@b Set the DC.} Apply your Method DC (see below) whenever a method requires a saving throw.
{@b Spend Stamina.} Activating a method consumes stamina (see below). Unless otherwise stated, you can use each method once per turn.
{@b Learn More.} Use the Methods Known column to track how many methods you learn and the Method Degree column for the highest degree you can select.
{@b Refresh and Replace.} Whenever you level and gain a new method, you may replace one method you know with another from a tradition you're proficient with.

entries.name: Stamina
entries: Your stamina pool equals twice your proficiency bonus and refreshes after a short or long rest.
Review {@variantrule Stamina|TGTT} for details on powering methods with stamina.

entries.name: Method DC
entries: Your Method DC equals 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice). Illriggers may instead use their Interdict save DC if preferred.
Consult {@variantrule Method DC|TGTT} for comprehensive rulings.

entries.name: Combat Tradition Rules
entries: Combat traditions determine your method options. Review {@variantrule Combat Traditions|TGTT} for tradition summaries and guidelines.

entries.name: Getting Started
entries: {@b Default Traditions.} For illriggers who balance dark power with tactical martial prowess, consider {@filter Eldritch Blackguard|optionalfeatures|feature type=CTM:EB} (fiendish combat techniques enhanced by dark magic) and {@filter Sanguine Knot|optionalfeatures|feature type=CTM:SK} (sacrificial techniques and protective abilities). This pairing reflects the illrigger's mastery of both infernal and martial power.

{@b Suggested Methods.} From Eldritch Blackguard, consider methods that combine weapon strikes with infernal energy. From Sanguine Knot, consider methods like {@optfeature Shield Wall|TGTT} (tactical defense) and {@optfeature Shoulder Check|TGTT} (repositioning enemies).

features.description:
At 2nd level, your infernal training expands into combat methods—martial techniques fueled by hellish stamina.

  • Choose Traditions. Gain proficiency in two combat traditions from Eldritch Blackguard, Gallant Heart, or Sanguine Knot. Learn two methods from traditions you're proficient with.
  • Set the DC. Apply your Method DC (see below) whenever a method requires a saving throw.
  • Spend Stamina. Activating a method consumes stamina (see below). Unless otherwise stated, you can use each method once per turn.
  • Learn More. Use the Methods Known column to track how many methods you learn and the Method Degree column for the highest degree you can select.
  • Refresh and Replace. Whenever you level and gain a new method, you may replace one method you know with another from a tradition you're proficient with.

Stamina[–]

Your stamina pool equals twice your proficiency bonus and refreshes after a short or long rest.

Review Stamina for details on powering methods with stamina.

Method DC[–]

Your Method DC equals 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice). Illriggers may instead use their Interdict save DC if preferred.

Consult Method DC for comprehensive rulings.

Combat Tradition Rules[–]

Combat traditions determine your method options. Review Combat Traditions for tradition summaries and guidelines.

Getting Started[–]

Default Traditions. For illriggers who balance dark power with tactical martial prowess, consider Eldritch Blackguard (fiendish combat techniques enhanced by dark magic) and Sanguine Knot (sacrificial techniques and protective abilities). This pairing reflects the illrigger's mastery of both infernal and martial power.

Suggested Methods. From Eldritch Blackguard, consider methods that combine weapon strikes with infernal energy. From Sanguine Knot, consider methods like Shield Wall (tactical defense) and Shoulder Check (repositioning enemies).

entries: Your archdevil grants you uncanny skill in a certain form of combat. Choose one of the following {@filter illrigger combat masteries|optionalfeatures|feature type=IllMastery}.

entries: You can infuse your seals with hellish magical power, enhancing their effects.

entries.name: Interdict Boons Known
entries: You learn one interdict boon of your choice from the "{@filter Interdict Boons|optionalfeatures|feature type=ItdBoon}" section. As you gain levels in this class, you gain additional boons of your choice, as shown in the Interdict Boons column of the Illrigger table. Each new boon must be of a level you can learn. When you reach 7th level, for example, you learn one new boon of 2nd or 7th level.
Whenever you gain an illrigger level, you can choose a boon you know and replace it with another boon you can learn.

entries.name: Using Interdict Boons
entries: Some boons allow you to expend unplaced seals to fuel abilities, while others empower all your seals or grant you benefits against interdicted creatures.

The boons that grant passive (or "always on") benefits, such as the 2nd-level Swift Retribution boon, are marked with a "Passive" tag. You don't need to expend a seal or take an action to benefit from the passive boons you know. All other boons, such as the 2nd-level Abating Seal boon, must be activated on a turn (for example, by expending a seal). You can activate only one non-passive boon per turn, regardless of how many you know.

entries.name: Burn vs. Expend
entries: Burning a seal is part of the main gameplay loop of this class. The illrigger places a seal by using a bonus action or hitting a creature with an attack, then burns the seal for additional damage (as described in the {@book Baleful Interdict|IllriggerRevised|0|Baleful Interdict} class feature). Many interdict boons activate when you burn a seal; these burned seals deal the normal damage to the interdicted creature in addition to any effects granted by the boon.

Other interdict boons instead require you to expend a seal. In this case, the illrigger expends an {@i unplaced} seal from their pool of available seals. This may require using an action, bonus action, or reaction, but not always (such as in the case of the Hellspeaker's {@book Charm Enemy|IllriggerRevised|0|Charm Enemy} feature, where you can expend seals to increase the number of targets).

Each active interdict boon details if any kind of action is required to expend the seal and activate the boon's benefit. Part of the illrigger's resource management is maximizing efficiency between burned seals (and their extra damage) and expended seals (and their unique effects).

features.name: Weapon Mastery
entries: Your training with weapons allows you to use the {@variantrule weapon mastery properties|XPHB|mastery properties} of two kinds of {@filter weapons|items|type=simple weapon;martial weapon} of your choice with which you have proficiency, such as {@item Longsword|XPHB|Longswords} and {@item Javelin|XPHB|Javelins}.

Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can change the kinds of weapons you chose. For example, you could switch to using the {@variantrule weapon mastery properties|XPHB|mastery properties} of {@item Halberd|XPHB|Halberds} and {@item Flail|XPHB|Flails}.
features.description:
Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of two kinds of weapons of your choice with which you have proficiency, such as Longswords and Javelins.

Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change the kinds of weapons you chose. For example, you could switch to using the mastery properties of Halberds and Flails.

features.name: Dark Resilience
entries: You gain resistance to fire damage. If you already have resistance to fire damage, you instead gain resistance to necrotic damage.
features.description: You gain resistance to fire damage. If you already have resistance to fire damage, you instead gain resistance to necrotic damage.

features.name: Invoke Hell
entries: Your diabolic connection allows you to channel infernal energy to fuel magical effects. Each Invoke Hell option provided by your archdevil contract describes how to use it. When you use your Invoke Hell, you choose which option to use.

You can use Invoke Hell twice. You regain one expended use when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You gain an additional use when you reach 11th level in this class.
Some Invoke Hell effects require a saving throw. When you use such an effect, the DC equals your interdict save DC.

features.name: Specialties
entries: Through your infernal training and diabolic contracts, you have developed specialized abilities that set you apart. You gain a specialty of your choice. You gain another specialty at 5th, 7th, 9th, 11th, 14th, and 19th level. Each specialty can only be selected once unless it says otherwise.

features.name: Hellspeaker
entries: {@i The charismatic and manipulative Hellspeakers serve Moloch as they slip about the battlefield, coercing enemies into becoming unwitting allies.}

Moloch rules Styx, the City of Lies, but his reach extends far beyond it. Hell's greatest politicians and diplomats rise to prominence through Moloch's subtle manipulations. They follow him with great loyalty, for they know they are nothing without him—and thus his power echoes through all of Hell.

Moloch's illriggers are silver-tongued enchanters, lulling his foes to complacency with sorcery and subterfuge until they wake and find themselves under the command of the Order of Desolation. These Hellspeakers train in the art known as the Red Cant or Hell's Cant. By understanding their enemy and through weaving subtle sorceries into normal speech, Hellspeakers can make their foes feel, think, or do nearly anything to accelerate Hell's victory.

Across the timescape, Hellspeakers enjoy a reputation as smiling rogues and swashbuckling villains. An asset in any negotiation, Hellspeakers know that in a world of lies, the truth can be as potent a weapon as steel.

entries.name: Content Warning
entries: This subclass has themes of mental manipulation and mind control. Before choosing this subclass, please ensure everyone at the table is comfortable exploring these dark and harmful themes. And as always, we encourage the ongoing use of safety tools throughout your game.

entries.name: Precepts of Deception
entries: Hellspeakers swear an oath to Moloch when they join the Order of Desolation. By following these precepts, they infiltrate the farthest reaches of power and manipulate all under their influence.

entries.name: My Voice Is a Weapon
entries: Even when my enchantments fail, if my enemy can hear me, they are mine.

entries.name: Doubt Is Certainty
entries: I need not convince my enemy, only sow doubt and wait for it to bear fruit.

entries.name: Trust Me
entries: For each lie I utter, I tell the truth tenfold. One who always lies says nothing.

entries.name: Never Tell the Same Lie Twice
entries: An overused skill becomes too predictable. Keep moving, switch targets, keep them guessing.

features.name: Moloch's Blessing
entries: When Moloch accepts you as his illrigger, you gain proficiency in the {@skill Persuasion} or {@skill Deception} skill (your choice). If you already have proficiency in the skill of your choice, your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make with that skill.

In addition, your Forked Tongue feature grants you an additional language (for a total of three at 3rd level and four at 9th level). Whenever you speak in a language gained by this feature, your devilish influence is subconsciously felt by creatures who can hear and understand you, granting you advantage on Charisma checks to influence those creatures.

features.name: Charm Enemy
entries: When you use your bonus action to place a seal on a Humanoid, you can attempt to charm them. The target must succeed on a Charisma saving throw or be {@condition charmed} by you for 1 hour or until you or your companions do anything harmful to them. While {@condition charmed}, the target regards you as a friendly acquaintance. When the {@condition charmed} condition ends, the target knows they were {@condition charmed} by you.

When you use this bonus action, you can additionally burn one or more seals on one or more other interdicted Humanoids within 30 feet of you, attempting to charm those targets as well. After taking damage from the burned seals, each of those targets must succeed on a Charisma saving throw or be under the same {@condition charmed} effect.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

entries: {@b Reaction (2 Stamina Points)}. Your grip can wither flesh from bone. When you are grappling an opponent, you can use your reaction to deal necrotic damage equal to {@dice 1d8} + your Charisma modifier in place of basic melee damage.

features.name: Purge Toxins
entries: {@i Prerequisite: 5th level}

You gain resistance to poison damage and advantage on saving throws against the {@condition poisoned} condition. Additionally, as an action you can spend 2 stamina to end one poison affecting you. If more than one poison is affecting you, you end one poison you know is present (otherwise you end one at random). You can end additional poisons with the same action by spending 1 additional stamina per poison.

features.name: Extra Attack
entries: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the {@action Attack} action on your turn.
features.description: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

features.name: Wink and Smile
entries: {@b Bonus Action (2 Stamina Points)}. A tossed rose, a blown kiss—you acknowledge someone whose eye was caught by your swagger. Choose one creature within 30 feet that can see you. Make a Performance check against the creature’s passive Insight. On a success, the creature is fixated on you until the start of your next turn.

features.name: Infernal Conduit
entries: You can strengthen your allies at the cost of yourself—or drain your enemy's life force for your own gain. You have a pool of Infernal Conduit dice, which are d10s. The number of Infernal Conduit dice in your pool increase as you gain illrigger levels, as shown in the Infernal Conduit Dice column of the Illrigger table.

As an action, you can touch another creature and spend one or more dice from your pool. The target must make a Constitution saving throw against your interdict save DC. A creature can willingly fail this saving throw. Roll the spent dice and choose one of the following effects:

entries.name: Invigorate
entries: On a failed save, the target regains hit points equal to the total you rolled, and you take necrotic damage equal to that total. On a successful save, the target regains half as many hit points, and you take necrotic damage equal to that total. Save or fail, this necrotic damage can't be reduced in any way, and if this damage reduces you to 0 hit points, you fall {@condition unconscious} and are stabilized.

entries.name: Devour
entries: On a failed save, the target takes necrotic damage equal to the total you rolled, and you regain hit points equal to that total. On a successful save, the target takes half as much damage, and you regain hit points equal to the damage the target took. Save or fail, or if the target chose to fail their saving throw against this effect, the necrotic damage can't be reduced in any way. When you reach 11th level in this class, the target also gains a level of {@condition exhaustion} on a failed save against this effect. This level of {@condition exhaustion} can be reduced as normal, and a creature can't suffer more than three levels of {@condition exhaustion} combined from all illriggers' Infernal Conduit features.
You regain any spent Infernal Conduit dice when you finish a long rest.

features.name: War God's Blessing
features.description: When a creature within 30 feet of you makes an attack roll, you can use your reaction to grant a +10 bonus to the roll, using your Channel Divinity. You make this choice after you see the roll, but before the DM says whether the attack hits or misses.

features.name: Veil of Lies
entries: As a bonus action, you can expend a seal to become {@condition invisible} for 10 minutes or until you attack or cast a spell.
features.description: As a bonus action, you can expend a seal to become invisible for 10 minutes or until you attack or cast a spell.

features.name: Infernal Awareness
entries: {@i Prerequisite: 7th level}

You gain {@sense blindsight} with a range of 10 feet—you can sense the presence of creatures through infernal perception. You may take this specialty a second time at 11th level or higher to extend the range to 30 feet.

features.name: Moloch's Interdiction
entries: You learn the following additional interdict boons at the noted illrigger levels. Once you learn an interdict boon granted by this feature, you always know it, and it doesn't count against the number of interdict boons you know.

features.name: Mistfade Retreat
entries: {@b Reaction (2 Stamina Points)}. As your foe’s deadly attack falls upon you, your form becomes mist and shadow. When you take damage from a melee attack, you can move 15 feet without provoking opportunity attacks.

features.name: Hellish Avenger
entries: {@i Prerequisite: 5th level}
Once per turn when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can deal an extra {@damage 1d8} fire damage. This damage increases to {@damage 2d8} at 11th level.
features.description:
Prerequisite: 5th level

features.name: Forked Tongue Improvement
entries: You can instinctively speak, read, and write Infernal.

In addition, you can speak two other languages of your choice, but you can't read or write them. When you finish a long rest, you can draw on your archdevil's knowledge to replace one of these two languages. When you do, choose another language whose name you know; you magically forget the previous language and gain this new one instead. Once you replace a language in this way, you must finish a long rest before you can do so again.

Starting at 9th level, this feature grants you another language, for a total of three (in addition to Infernal). Furthermore, you gain advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) checks made to ascertain the intentions or sincerity of creatures.

features.name: To My Side
entries: {@b Action (2 Stamina Points)}. You beckon someone to your side with infectious fervor, be they stranger or comrade-in-arms. Choose one conscious non-hostile creature within 30 feet of you that can see you. The creature can use its reaction to move up to its Speed in a straight line toward you. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks. If the creature enters your reach, you can use your reaction to draw one item and administer it to the creature if it is willing. The item must be a potion, medicine, or some other beneficial consumable.

features.name: Blood Price
entries: You can strengthen your defenses at the cost of your vitality. Whenever you fail a saving throw, you can spend one of your Hit Dice, rolling it and adding the number rolled to the result of the save.
features.description: You can strengthen your defenses at the cost of your vitality. Whenever you fail a saving throw, you can spend one of your Hit Dice, rolling it and adding the number rolled to the result of the save.

feats.name: Bountiful Luck
feats.description:
Your people have extraordinary luck, which you have learned to mystically lend to your companions when you see them falter. You're not sure how you do it; you just wish it, and it happens. Surely a sign of fortune's favor!

When an ally you can see within 30 feet of you rolls a 1 on the d20 for an attack roll, an ability check, or a saving throw, you can use your reaction to let the ally reroll the die. The ally must use the new roll.

When you use this ability, you can't use your Lucky racial trait before the end of your next turn.
